title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: Understanding Median Salary and State Differences

faqs.q: What is the formula to convert hourly to annual?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week (usually 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual: The Basics

To turn your hourly rate into an annual salary, use the standard formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, that’s hourly × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Multiply by 38 hours and 52 weeks: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,270.72 per year. Your fortnightly gross pay would be roughly $2,010.41 (annual ÷ 26).

This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It’s a starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

### Why 38 Hours?

The 38-hour week is the standard full-time week under the Fair Work Act. Many awards and agreements use it as the base. If you work different hours, adjust the formula accordingly. For part-time or casual work, use your actual weekly hours.

## Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage (NMW) is set by the Fair Work Commission and applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, it’s $26.44 per hour. But most workers are covered by an award or registered agreement that sets a higher minimum rate for their industry or role.

Award rates vary by classification and often include penalty rates for weekends, nights, or public holidays. The NMW is a floor, not a target. If you’re on an award, your minimum hourly rate will be higher.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate (or award rate) to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the NMW, that’s $33.05 per hour casual. Our [timesheet](/) lets you add casual loading with a checkbox—never type a rate that already includes it.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

While the NMW is national, ordinary-time earnings vary significantly across states and territories. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings survey for May 2026 shows full-time adult ordinary-time earnings at $2,083.70 per week nationally. But state-level data reveals clear differences.

Workers in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory typically earn above the national average, while those in Tasmania and South Australia tend to earn below. Victoria, Queensland, and Western Australia sit closer to the middle, though mining states can push averages higher.

These state differences affect the **median salary** in each region. The median salary is the middle point—half of workers earn more, half earn less. It’s often a better benchmark than the average because it’s less skewed by very high earners. For example, the median salary in the ACT is higher than in Tasmania, reflecting the concentration of public service and professional roles.

If you’re comparing your pay to a median salary for your occupation, remember that state matters. The ABS publishes median salary data by occupation and state, but we don’t have a specific median for your job here. Use our [reference tables](/data) to see industry or state averages—but note these are averages, not medians for your exact role.

## Tax and Super Considerations

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. Tax and super change the picture.

### Income Tax 2026–27

The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) resident tax rates for 2026–27 are:
- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (generally). The tax-free threshold is included. Our calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare because the 2026–27 thresholds weren’t confirmed here. This is an estimate, not a determination of your tax.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Employers must pay super on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% from 1 July 2026, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay—it’s an extra cost for the employer. For example, on a $60,000 salary, super adds $7,200 per year to your total remuneration.

Our [super and packaging page](/topics/super-and-packaging) explains how salary packaging and the super cap work. Remember, the calculator estimates super at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the maximum contribution base.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) is the home page. Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and choose your weekly hours. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading if you’re casual. The calculator then shows:
- Annual gross pay (hourly × hours × 52)
- Fortnightly and weekly amounts
- Estimated tax and Medicare levy
- Estimated super on top

It’s a quick way to compare a salary offer to your current hourly rate, or to see what a pay rise means annually. Always check your award or agreement for exact rates and conditions.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Final Thoughts

Understanding your annual equivalent helps you negotiate and budget. The median salary in your state and occupation gives context, but your personal circumstances—hours, casual status, super, and tax—determine your real take-home pay. Use our tools to get a clearer picture.
